definitions.definition: R=ℤ_(p)={a/b∈ℚ:a,b∈ℤ, b≠0, p does not divide b}, with the usual rational arithmetic and its embedding into ℂ.
M_R=R⊗_ℤ M. Once its multiplication map into V is proved injective, it is identified with its image in V.
ι_R is the tensor multiplication map determined by ι_R(r⊗m)=r m for r∈R and m∈M, using the rational scalar action on V.

inputs.statement: n>0. All the R-submodules Jcoord_i (i∈I) equal J. J is nonzero and finitely generated over R. Inside V one has M_R=⊕_{i∈I}J e_i: explicitly every element of M_R has a unique expression ∑_{i∈I}c_i e_i with c_i∈J, and every such finite sum belongs to M_R. Put T=ℚ⊗_R J. The multiplication map T→ℂ, q⊗c↦qc, is injective, T is finite dimensional over ℚ and dim_ℚ T=1. For every nonzero a∈J and every c∈J there exists q∈ℚ with c=qa.

output.statement: There exists b∈J with b≠0 such that J=Rb. For any such b, the vectors (b e_i)_{i∈I} form an R-basis of M_R (identified with its image under ι_R), of cardinality n>0.

argument.text: N003 says J is nonzero and finitely generated. Remove all zero members of a finite generating family. The remaining family still generates, and cannot be empty because J≠0. This proves F001, which will allow the finite minimum construction.

produces.statement: There exists a nonempty finite family of nonzero elements generating J as an R-module.

argument.text: Choose a≠0 in J and a family g as in F001. By the rational-line conclusion of N003, every g_j is q_j a for some q_j∈ℚ; because g_j and a are nonzero, q_j≠0. For a nonzero rational q=A/B with nonzero integers A,B, repeatedly remove factors p from A and B. This process terminates since p≥2 by H001 and absolute values strictly decrease at each removal. Thus A=p^s A', B=p^t B' with s,t≥0 and p dividing neither A' nor B'. Consequently q=p^{s-t}(A'/B'), where A'/B' is a unit of R: both A'/B' and its inverse B'/A' satisfy the denominator condition. Apply this to all the finitely many nonzero rational coefficients of g relative to a. For each there is an integer exponent and a unit of R; the nonempty finite list of exponents has a minimum and an index attaining it. These are precisely the existential data in F002.

produces.statement: There exist families q0,u0,η0 indexed by the chosen nonempty finite family g, a minimum κ0∈ℤ and an index jmin of g such that every q0_j is a nonzero rational, every u0_j is a unit of R, every η0_j is an integer, g_j=q0_j a=p^{η0_j}u0_j a, κ0≤η0_j for every j, and η0_jmin=κ0.

argument.text: Choose simultaneously from F002 the exponent family νexp (entries ν_j), the unit family u, the minimum ν and an attaining index j_0. Put b=p^ν a=u_{j_0}^{-1}g_{j_0}. This is a nonzero element of J, since p^ν is a nonzero rational and a≠0. Every generator g_j equals p^{ν_j-ν}u_j b with ν_j-ν≥0, so g_j∈Rb; conversely b∈J gives Rb⊂J. Therefore J=Rb. Substituting into the unique-coordinate decomposition of N003 proves that every element of M_R is a unique R-linear combination of b e_i: if ∑r_i b e_i=0, N003 gives r_i b=0 for each i, hence r_i=0 since b≠0. Thus these vectors are an R-basis indexed by I, of cardinality n>0. The same argument applies to any nonzero b∈J with J=Rb, proving the full principal-generator and basis assertion.
